title: Punctuation and commands
goal: Marks, capitals and editing keys are assigned before any word, so no word takes their strokes.

blocks.x: Punctuation, commands and fingerspelling are reserved ahead of every word; a word that wanted a reserved stroke takes its next-cheapest outline. These strokes are the same everywhere.
Every mark and command has exactly one stroke. A mark that spaces differently (the hyphen that joins words, the one with a space round it) is a different mark with its own stroke.

[[KPA]] capitalises the next word and keeps the space; [[KPA*]] does the same, glued to the word before. Names: strike the sound-alike outline after a capital stroke. Shortcut, the name lane: strike `#` alone (types nothing), then the same outline; the name comes out capitalised (`#`, then `TKAPBL` is *Daniel*). A name the dictionary lacks is read from names alone ([the name lane](#/ref/names)).
Add the star to a movement stroke to **select** while moving: [[STPH*R]] is Shift+Left. `STPH` is the family; the right-hand keys give the direction.

Movement strokes and Backspace fire when the **first** key comes up, not the last: **hold** `STPH` and tap `-R`, `-R`, `-R` to walk the cursor left, then tap `-P` to go up, without lifting. Needs Keymux; the [reference page](#/ref/punctuation/send-on-the-first-key-up) has the full list and the one trap.
F1 to F12 are `TPW` plus the number's own sound: [[TPWUPB]] is F1, [[TPWO]] is F2.
